rules.heading: ## The owner's messages
rules.quote: An agent cannot run the status command, and a search over the transcript cannot tell the owner's messages from the harness's own text.
rules.says: An agent cannot run the status command, and a plain search over the transcript cannot distinguish the owner's messages from the harness's own text, so the owner's messages must be read with the script given here.

rules.heading: ## The owner's messages
rules.quote: The transcript is `/root/.claude/projects/-home-user/<session id>.jsonl`, the session id being the third path component of the scratchpad.
rules.says: The session transcript is at /root/.claude/projects/-home-user/<session id>.jsonl, where the session id is the third path component of the scratchpad path.

rules.heading: ## The owner's messages
rules.quote: Write the script below to a file in the scratchpad's `scratch` folder with the Write tool, and run it with node.
rules.says: To read the owner's messages, an agent writes the script below with the Write tool to a file in the scratchpad's scratch folder and runs it with node.

rules.heading: ## The owner's messages
rules.quote: It carries its own control and prints it first. It exits 0 whatever it finds.
rules.says: The script carries its own control, prints it before anything else, and exits 0 whatever it finds.

rules.heading: ## The owner's messages
rules.quote: `--messages` prints each owner message typed before the cutoff, with its California time and its text.
rules.says: The --messages option prints each owner message typed before the cutoff, with its California time and its text.

rules.heading: ## The owner's messages
rules.quote: The cutoff is `--before-step N` (the newest end of step N) or, without it, no cutoff.
rules.says: The cutoff for --messages is --before-step N, meaning the newest end of step N, and with no such option there is no cutoff.

rules.heading: ## The owner's messages
rules.quote: A message is placed by the time it was TYPED, not the time it was delivered.
rules.says: An owner message is placed in time by when it was typed, never by when it was delivered.

rules.heading: ## The owner's messages
rules.quote: `--floor "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM"` goes with `--messages`: a California date and time before which nothing is printed, so a review reads the messages from the moment its plan's aim began and not the whole session.
rules.says: The --floor option, used with --messages and given as a California date and time, prints nothing typed before it, so a review reads messages from when its plan's aim began rather than the whole session; a message typed at the floor itself is printed.

rules.heading: ## The owner's messages
rules.quote: A floor written in any other form is said so, and is not applied.
rules.says: A floor not written as YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM California time is reported as such and is not applied.

rules.heading: ## The owner's messages
rules.quote: The control proves the floor before anything is printed: it checks the conversion of a California time to an instant on both sides of the change between summer and winter time, and that planted messages typed before the floor are dropped and those typed from it are kept.
rules.says: Before printing anything, the script's control must prove the floor by checking the California-time conversion on both sides of the summer/winter change and that planted messages before the floor are dropped and those from it are kept.

rules.heading: ## The owner's messages
rules.quote: `--judged <plan path>` prints the step of the newest end of an agent for a step in the plan's Order, which is N.
rules.says: The --judged <plan path> option prints the step N, being the step of the newest end of an agent for a step in the plan's Order.

rules.heading: ## The owner's messages
rules.quote: // owner-messages.mjs: the owner's messages of a session, by the time each was typed, and the step the review judges. Prints its control first.
rules.says: The script to write and run is the given owner-messages.mjs, which imports the hub's transcript-tail, hook-dispatch and report modules, prints its control first, reads the transcript, and supports --messages, --before-step, --floor and --judged, with owner messages placed by typed time, printed in California time, and exiting 0.

rules.heading: ## The owner's messages
rules.quote: console.log('MADE TO FAIL: the planted transcript holds 3 owner messages, 2 of them typed before second 15 and all 3 before second 25
rules.says: The script's output is trustworthy only if its control line prints 3 messages, 2 typed before second 15 and 3 typed before second 25.

rules.heading: ## The owner's messages
rules.quote: console.log('MADE TO FAIL (the floor): the California time 2026-10-01 05:30 is 12:30 UTC and 2026-12-01 04:00 is 12:00 UTC
rules.says: The script's output is trustworthy only if its floor control line prints 12:30, 12:00, 2 and 0.

rules.heading: ## The owner's messages
rules.says: The script reads the transcript only when given its path as an argument ending in .jsonl; without it only the control is printed and neither --messages nor --judged prints anything.

rules.heading: ## The owner's messages
rules.says: --judged prints the step, its end time in California time and how it ended, or the line 'judged: none (no step of Order has ended)' when no step of the plan's Order has ended.

rules.heading: ## The owner's messages
rules.says: With --before-step, the cutoff is taken only from a report-type end of that step, and if no report of the step is found the script says so and applies no cutoff.
